title: Aurora Bank - SIG / CAIQ & Evidence Walkthrough
next_steps: Maya to share filled CAIQ CSV and link to latest SOC 2 Type II report by 2025-04-10
Omar to run 45-minute technical deep dive (audit logs, KMS walk-through) week of 2025-04-14
Aurora InfoSec to provide prioritized questions from their vendor team by 2025-04-11
action_items: Maya: Upload SOC 2 redacted report + ISO27001 statement to secure link; due 2025-04-10
Omar: Prepare short demo showing export of audit logs (S3 + syslog) and RBAC screens; due 2025-04-15

meeting_header: Date: 2025-04-08 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47m\nAttendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Alice Rivera (Aurora InfoSec), Ben Thompson (CTO), Lina Gomez (Procurement)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood's responses to Aurora's SIG/CAIQ and evidence request process. Covered SOC 2/ISO posture, SSO/RBAC integration (Okta), audit log exports, KMS/HSM key management and key rotation, and data residency options including Private/VPC deployments. Agreed next steps: provide SOC 2 report, completed CAIQ CSV, schedule technical deep dive focused on audit logs and KMS evidence.
topics: SOC 2 Type II availability and redaction rules
SSO/SAML with Okta and SCIM provisioning
RBAC roles and least privilege in Redwood Console
Audit logs: retention, export formats, and SIEM integrations
Encryption at rest/in-transit and KMS/HSM support
Data residency and Private deployment options
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this deal, with me is Omar, our solutions engineer.
00:08 Alice Rivera: Hi Maya, hi Omar, Alice here — I'm the InfoSec manager at Aurora. Ben and Lina are on as well.
00:15 Ben Thompson: Hey all. Quick note — procurement wants us to move through the SIG/CAIQ items today and then follow up with evidence.
00:22 Omar Patel: Great. So the agenda: we'll step through our CAIQ answers at a high level, call out where we attach evidence (SOC2, pen test, network diagrams), and then cover questions on SSO, RBAC, logs, and KMS.
00:35 Maya Chen: Also, quick note: some items in the CAIQ are answered by linking to our compliance pack instead of re-uploading the same doc repeatedly — saves time.
00:42 Alice Rivera: That's fine, but procurement needs a direct link to the documents and a primary point of contact for evidence.
00:49 Omar Patel: Understood. For primary contacts, Maya will be the commercial contact and I'll be the technical lead for evidence.
00:55 Lina Gomez: From procurement, we need to confirm minimal redaction rules for SOC2 and SLA language — what are typical redactions?
01:02 Maya Chen: We normally allow customer name redaction on SOC 2 but not the control narratives. We can provide a fully redacted PII layer if required; we also provide a signed attestation around the redactions.
01:14 Alice Rivera: And ISO? Do you have ISO27001 certificate?
01:18 Omar Patel: We maintain an ISO statement of applicability and an auditor's certificate for our private control plane customers; for hosted customers we provide the ISO attestation where applicable. If Aurora needs the cert, we'll share the scanned cert with redactions as needed.
01:30 Ben Thompson: Great. On CAIQ, question A.2.1 asks about key management. Can you explain how keys are stored and rotated?
01:38 Omar Patel: Sure — for the hosted Redwood API we use envelope encryption. Customer data is encrypted at rest with AES-256; the data encryption key is itself encrypted by a master key managed in the cloud KMS. We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private via KMS integrations — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and we have an HSM-backed option for on-prem. Key rotation policies are configurable; default rotation 90 days, we can attest to rotation logs.
02:05 Alice Rivera: How do you provide evidence of key rotation? The auditor team wants rotation logs and a mapping of key IDs to rotation events.
02:12 Omar Patel: We can export key rotation logs from our control plane; for BYOK customers the KMS provider's rotation logs are the source of truth. We'll provide CSV exports or sign off statements plus hashed references.
02:24 Alice Rivera: Ok. For audit logs — retention and export — we need a 12-month retention for security events and ability to stream to our SIEM.
02:33 Omar Patel: We support configurable retention; default retained logs are 90 days in the platform but for enterprise customers we provide longer retention via dedicated buckets (S3) or log forwarders to your syslog/SIEM. For Aurora, we can configure 12 months retention and set up a streaming syslog endpoint or S3 export with lifecycle rules.
02:49 Ben Thompson: And log contents — do we log caller identity, model used, prompt metadata? We need to know what PII risks exist in logs.
02:59 Omar Patel: We capture request metadata: request ID, timestamp, auth subject (user/role), model identifier, latency, and token counts. We don't log raw prompt content by default into the long-term audit store; prompt/response bodies are retained in a short-lived KV cache for 24–72 hours depending on config for debugging, but can be disabled or redacted for compliance.
03:21 Alice Rivera: That 24–72 window is a concern. Can you disable storing prompts entirely for our account?
03:27 Omar Patel: Yes, we can enable a strict no-persist policy — prompt and output bodies will not be stored beyond the ephemeral processing pipeline. We'll reflect that flag in the CAIQ and provide an app config screenshot as evidence.
03:39 Lina Gomez: On SSO: you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM OK?
03:44 Maya Chen: Correct, SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We have a pre-built Okta integration and a generic SAML config if you use another IdP.
03:52 Alice Rivera: For RBAC, will we be able to enforce least privilege? We need role separation between developers and security ops.
03:59 Omar Patel: The Redwood Console has role-based access control with built-in roles (Admin, Operator, ReadOnly) and custom roles. You can scope roles to projects and model routes. We can show a screenshot during the tech deep dive.
04:14 Ben Thompson: Does RBAC integrate with groups from Okta?
04:18 Omar Patel: Yes, SCIM will sync groups and you can map groups to roles.
04:22 Alice Rivera: About data residency — Aurora needs EU data at rest and EU processing for a subset of accounts. Can Redwood guarantee data stays in the EU region?
04:31 Maya Chen: We offer region pinning on our Dedicated and Private tiers. For hosted customers we can route requests to EU buckets and EU regions; we can commit to region residency SLA for Dedicated. We'll document the routing policy and how backups are handled.
04:44 Lina Gomez: And the CAIQ asks for network diagrams and segmentation. Do you have a standard diagram?
04:49 Omar Patel: Yes — we'll attach our network architecture diagram and a redacted VPC layout. For Private deployments we include the on-prem architecture. We'll attach those as evidence links in the CAIQ.
04:59 Alice Rivera: Pen test coverage — frequency and whether third‑party tests are available.
05:04 Maya Chen: We run annual third‑party penetration tests and continuous vuln scanning. We can share the exec summary and remediation timelines; full reports are available under NDA.
05:14 Ben Thompson: Is there a Service Organization Control (SOC) 2 Type II report?
05:19 Maya Chen: Yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II covering the hosted control environment through 2024; we'll provide a redacted copy and the scope statement.
05:27 Alice Rivera: Will that include any 3PAAS vendors? We need to map subservice organizations.
05:32 Omar Patel: The SOC 2 includes a list of major vendors (cloud provider, monitoring, SSO provider). We'll provide the subservice organization list relevant to the controls.
05:40 Lina Gomez: Procurement wonders about indemnity clauses related to data breaches. Not sure you can do much live but can you flag if Redwood accepts carve-outs?
05:48 Maya Chen: We'll provide standard commercial terms; exceptions are handled through legal, but we can share our standard redlines and review with our legal team if Aurora submits specific language.
05:57 Alice Rivera: On the CAIQ, there are a bunch of technical evidence asks like network ACLs, WAF config, access logs. What's the recommended artifact list to speed up review?
06:08 Omar Patel: Recommended artifacts: SOC 2 report, network diagram, pen test exec summary, KMS key rotation logs, sample audit export (CSV), SSO metadata XML, RBAC role mapping screenshot, and our data flow diagram. We'll attach direct links for each CAIQ question where applicable.
06:24 Ben Thompson: For evidence delivery — can you upload artifacts to our secure folder or you want to push to a signed S3 share?
06:31 Maya Chen: We prefer to share via secure signed links (time-limited) or via your secure portal if you provide one. We can also push to an S3 bucket with limited access if that's easier for Aurora.
06:41 Alice Rivera: If you send a CAIQ CSV, can you align the column "evidence_uri" to the attachments so the reviewers don't have to hunt?
06:49 Omar Patel: Yes, we'll populate the CAIQ CSV with direct evidence links and a short note about redactions.
06:55 Lina Gomez: A quick question — your private offering, does it come with a separate control plane?
07:01 Omar Patel: For Private we ship a customer‑managed control plane; API keys and operational logs are in your VPC. That gives you more control for residency and auditability.
07:10 Alice Rivera: Ok good. How do you handle change control? Aurora requires documented change approvals for infra changes affecting security controls.
07:19 Omar Patel: We have a change management ticketing workflow and SOR (system of record) with approvals. We can export change tickets and attach proof of approvals for major changes as evidence.
07:28 Ben Thompson: For the technical follow-up, can Omar show an example of exporting logs and the RBAC UI, and walk through a KMS rotation event?
07:36 Omar Patel: Absolutely — I'll prepare a short demo. I'll also export a sample CSV of rotation events and a sample Syslog stream.
07:44 Alice Rivera: Anything in CAIQ about model hallucinations or content risk? We want to know how you monitor for model drift and unsafe outputs.
07:52 Omar Patel: We have content monitors, configurable classifiers, and can route risky calls to lower‑capability models or human review. Our quality monitoring in Redwood Optimize flags regressions and can tie to prompt test suites. We'll attach our eval summary and monitoring policies.
08:07 Maya Chen: Recap — we'll share the CAIQ CSV with evidence links, SOC 2 redacted, pen test exec summary, key rotation logs, and schedule the technical deep dive.
08:16 Alice Rivera: Sounds good. We'll prioritize 10 CAIQ items that are blockers and send them to you.
08:21 Ben Thompson: From my side, please include the region residency options and any SLA language for Dedicated deployments.
08:28 Lina Gomez: Procurement will expect a timeline to finalize the legal review once we get the evidence.
08:33 Maya Chen: Noted — we'll aim to get the pack to you by Friday.
08:36 Alice Rivera: Great. Thanks everyone.
08:39 Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and next meeting invite.
08:43 (call ends)
